A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same metacognition study. All 25 pages of v1 and 26 pages of v2, including their appendices, support comparison. Existing figures and tables can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM experiments using the Delegate Game and Second Chance Game, baseline accuracy measurements, token-probability analyses, and supplementary controls.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds prompt-sensitivity, seed-sensitivity, and decision-only delegation experiments in Appendices A.11–A.12.

M1.justification: Appendix A.12 adds a procedural adaptation of the Delegate Game: models output an Answer/Delegate decision token and are told that answering will occur subsequently. The original game instead requires an actual answer or delegation token. The two primary paradigms otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use GPQA, its short-answer variant GPSA, SimpleQA, and its multiple-choice variant SimpleMC for factual and reasoning metacognition tasks. The added controls vary sampling, prompts, and response procedures within this coverage.

E2.justification: The neutral-prompt baseline for the Second Chance Game and Appendix A.10 comparisons with self-reported confidence and the Pass Game are retained. The new analyses examine variants of the existing games rather than introduce additional competing methods.

E3.justification: Appendices A.11–A.12 add experimental conditions involving resampled teammate histories and test questions, a less exhortatory Second Chance prompt, and decision-only delegation on selected models. Existing experimental protocols are retained; the newly stated temperatures clarify documentation rather than establish changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: Three new controls substantially expand validation of the metacognition interpretation: sensitivity to question-history sampling, sensitivity to Second Chance prompt strength, and whether delegation correlations persist without competition between answer and delegation tokens. These analyses appear in Figures 23–25 and were absent from v1.

E5.justification: Appendix A.11 newly reports rerunning selected Delegate Game evaluations with different random seeds and pooling results in Figure 23. Seed values and run counts are unspecified. Bootstrap confidence intervals and significance reporting were already present; no replacement of those procedures is documented.

E6.justification: Existing reported results are retained, while Figures 23–25 add results under the supplementary conditions. Examples include pooled SimpleMC correlations of 0.17 for Sonnet 4 and 0.21 for Grok 3, and a decision-only SimpleMC correlation of 0.22 for GPT-4o. Figure 24 adds prompt-dependent answer-change rates. These are additional-condition results, not revised same-setting performance scores.

T1.justification: The normalized change-rate definition, partial-correlation framework, and teammate-weighted and probability-weighted confidence formulas in Appendix A.4 are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, proofs, or mathematical derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claims remain unchanged: recent LLMs exhibit limited, context-dependent confidence monitoring and self-modeling, with possible effects of post-training. The added controls support these retained claims without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly acknowledges that learned knowledge of question-type difficulty and mechanical answer-token competition could mimic introspection. It discusses evidence against these explanations, while Appendix A.12 acknowledges reduced effects and possible confusion from the decision-only formulation. Existing limitations concerning context dependence and weak metacognitive performance remain.

D1.justification: Sections 2.4–2.5 newly specify temperature 0 for delegation decisions and connect Second Chance temperatures to Section 2.3. Appendix A.11 describes the exact prompt edits. Replication details remain incomplete: seed counts are absent, and Figure 24 labels a Gemini 2.5 Flash preview endpoint differently from Table 1. The source-code availability statement is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lindsey (2025) and two Song et al. (2025) works. It relates its approach to privileged self-access definitions of introspection and connects its context-dependent findings to these studies, while retaining the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds localized explanations of self-report limitations and model selection, expands the discussion with a limitations paragraph, and appends Sections A.11–A.12. The overall narrative and section order remain stable, with minor wording corrections and an ICLR publication header.

P2.justification: The model inventory is converted from prose into a new Table 1, and Figures 23–25 are added. Existing tables are renumbered and some figures relocate during reflow. The original figure images remain identical, and the overall visual design is retained.

improvement.justification: The added controls in Appendices A.11–A.12 address previously untested prompt sensitivity and answer-token competition, modestly strengthening support for the unchanged conclusions. The expanded limitations discussion and temperature disclosures also improve transparency. The gains remain limited by selected-model coverage and incomplete documentation of seeds and the model identifier used in Figure 24.
